// Grammar for the rule language. The parser module calc/_parser.py is generated from this file.
?start: expr
?expr: expr "+" term   -> add
     | expr "-" term   -> sub
     | term
?term: term "*" atom   -> mul
     | term "/" atom   -> div
     | atom
?atom: NUMBER          -> num
     | "true"          -> true
     | "false"         -> false
     | "(" expr ")"
NUMBER: /[0-9]+/
%ignore " "

gen:
	python -m lark.tools.standalone calc/grammar.lark > calc/_parser.py

test:
	python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

turns.content:
The issue was caused by the `NUMBER` rule in `calc/grammar.lark` only matching integers (`/[0-9]+/`). I updated the rule to support decimal numbers by allowing an optional decimal point followed by digits. I also ensured the parser was regenerated correctly.

The fix involved:
1.  Updating `calc/grammar.lark`:
    ```lark
    NUMBER: /([0-9]*\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)/
    ```
2.  Regenerating the parser using `make gen` (or the equivalent manual command).

Tests now pass successfully.
